chain.label: Single-panel rudder with single PCU and no jam-tolerant redundancy
chain.trigger: the 737 is the only twin wing-mounted engine, large transport-category airplane designed with a single rudder panel and single rudder actuator

chain.label: 737-300 derivative certification retained 1967 rudder criteria without 25.671 jam analysis
chain.trigger: the certification basis for those airplanes consisted primarily of the same certification requirements and design criteria that existed for the original -100 and -200 series airplanes

chain.label: Main rudder PCU servo valve secondary slide jammed to housing offset from neutral
chain.trigger: a jam of the main rudder power control unit servo valve secondary slide to the servo valve housing offset from its neutral position

caused_by.evidence: tight diametric clearances of the dual-concentric servo valve; secondary slide jammed to the servo valve housing
Boeing indicated that in the event of a jamming failure that immobilizes the rudder system, yaw control can be maintained through the use of lateral control

chain.label: Wake vortex encounter from preceding Delta 727 produces yaw/roll upset
chain.trigger: USAir flight 427 most likely encountered the wake vortices produced by Delta flight 1083 about the time of the initial upset

chain.label: Crew right rudder pedal input to counter the wake-induced left yaw
chain.trigger: the flight crew responded to the nose left yawing motion with a right rudder pedal input about 1903:00

caused_by.evidence: the wake vortex produced a nose left heading change... this simulation assumed that the flight crew responded to the nose left yawing motion with a right rudder pedal input

chain.label: Primary slide overtravel causes reverse rudder response to left blowdown limit
chain.trigger: The rudder surface most likely deflected in a direction opposite to that commanded by the pilots as a result of a jam... and overtravel of the primary slide

caused_by.evidence: when the secondary slide was jammed to the servo valve housing at certain positions, the primary slide could travel beyond its intended stop position
the flight crew's rudder pedal input resulted in a rudder motion reversal, with the rudder reaching its blowdown limit (about 12.5 degrees) about 1903:00

chain.label: Airspeed 190 knots at flaps 1 near crossover airspeed, roll authority insufficient
chain.trigger: the roll could not be completely eliminated (and control of the airplane could not be regained) by using full control wheel inputs if the airspeed remained below 187 KCAS

caused_by.evidence: the rudder has to be sufficiently powerful... roll authority (using spoilers and ailerons) was not sufficient to completely counter the roll effects of a rudder deflected to its blowdown limit

chain.label: No unusual attitude or rudder-upset recovery training available to the crew
chain.trigger: the training being conducted did not include recovery from unusual attitudes or upsets

chain.label: Aft control column increases load factor and crossover airspeed, worsening roll
chain.trigger: the control column had started to move aft... an increase in vertical load factor, or angle-of-attack, resulted in an increase in the crossover airspeed

caused_by.evidence: the airplane had begun to descend from its assigned altitude of 6,000 feet msl, the control column had started to move aft
pilots who participated... reported that recovery required prompt control wheel inputs and pitch inputs to maintain a speed above the crossover airspeed

chain.label: Aerodynamic stall with stickshaker activation at about 1903:08
chain.trigger: a vibrating sound similar to aircraft stickshaker started and continued until the end of the recording

caused_by.evidence: the FDR recorded increasing left roll, aft control column, decreasing altitude, and a decreasing airspeed to about 186 knots

chain.label: Uncontrolled left roll and descent from 6,000 feet
chain.trigger: The airplane entered an uncontrolled descent and impacted terrain near Aliquippa, Pennsylvania

caused_by.evidence: the probable cause... was a loss of control of the airplane resulting from the movement of the rudder surface to its blowdown limit
at airspeeds of 187 KCAS and below, the roll induced by a full rudder deflection could not be completely eliminated by full control wheel input
The airplane entered an aerodynamic stall about 1903:08 and rolled more rapidly to the left
